newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE launches one-month Euromark futures contract.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE launches one-month Euromark futures contract.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) launched a one-month Euromark interest rate futures contract on Thursday, less than two weeks after a rival contract was launched in Germany.

Earlier this month, German exchange Deutsche Terminboerse (DTB) introduced its own one-month Euromark contract in an attempt to woo some of the business in mark contracts currently transacted in London. A three-month contract follows in January.
"This is a further step in our EMU strategy," said LIFFE's chairman Jack Wigglesworth at a presentation after the opening bell for the contract. "LIFFE...has to stay ahead of the game."
DTB board member Joerg Franke said earlier in the month he expected the German exchange to gain more than 50 percent of trading volume in the new one-month future.

But LIFFE chief executive Daniel Hodson said LIFFE's new one-month contract would complement its existing three-month Euromark futures, which is the most liquid short-term interest rate future in Europe.
"We believe the depth provided by open outcry is bound to prove more attractive. The German (one-month) contract has already seen volume falling off," Hodson said.
Euromark futures on LIFFE traded a new record daily volume in October, trading more than 3.77 million contracts during the month.
LIFFE's managing director of business development, Ralf Herklotz, said LIFFE's dominance in the three-month contract would mean the one-month contract attracted more trade than its DTB rival.
"Investors offset three-months against one-month, and LIFFE has a clear commercial advantage in the mark area," he said.
He said LIFFE would be keeping a watch on the level of open interest over the next three months to gauge the performance of the new contract.
"We expect it to be smaller than the three-month," he said. "But strong open interest is important for its success. We'd like to see people using it as a hedging tool."
Morgan Grenfell and Chase are market-makers for the new contract, LIFFE said.
On the floor, activity at the start of the one-month Euromark trading session was brisk, with December 1996 and May 1997 contracts proving active.
A major French house was seen buying December contracts early in the session, while spread trade between February and May was also popular for one major British brokerage.
December one-month Euromark futures were trading at 96.74 by 1020 GMT. More than 3,000 December contracts were traded, and more than 4,200 of May.
